results.gap_diagnosis: The coverage is bottlenecked because the teacher is doing most of the talking, and there is no evidence of students generating knowledge or outputs on their own. For example, the teacher could ask students to reflect on their own project progress and write down what they have accomplished so far, and what they still need to work on.
results.scaffolding_strategy: Two possible strategies are: (1) 'Individual Project Status Reflection': ask each student to write a brief reflection on their current project status, including what they have completed and what challenges they are facing. This will allow students to construct their own understanding of their project progress. (2) 'Solo Project Planning': provide each student with a project planning template, and ask them to fill it out individually, outlining their goals, tasks, and timeline for the project. This will enable students to generate their own project plan and take ownership of their learning.
